weeklyPage.title: This week’s adventure
weeklyPage.subtitle: Bluey-style bite-sized stories that blend online safety with AI literacy. One week at a time.
weeklyPage.previewBeforeLaunch: Season 1 preview — week 1 is live while we count down to launch day.
weeklyPage.cappedNote: You’re caught up! This is our latest published week. More adventures arrive soon.

1.title: SpArki’s Kind Grid
1.tagline: Photos, feelings, and pausing before you post.
1.story: SpArki opens a glowing photo grid — some squares make friends smile, and some feel too loud. This week, kids practice noticing what’s kind to share, when to pause, and how grown-ups can help. When AI is part of the learning, ask a grown-up to help you check—AI can be wrong.
1.parentBlurb: Theme: Instagram-style sharing and emotional safety. Ask: “What would you show Grandma?” Tie it to the Safety unit, then explore how AI learns from examples in the AI unit. Remember: AI can be wrong, so ask a grown-up to help you check AI ideas.

2.title: Short Videos, Big Feelings
2.tagline: Fast clips, kind comments, healthy breaks.
2.story: SpArki’s feed zips by like fireflies. Kids learn that quick videos can be fun — and that our brains need breaks, kind words, and a plan when something feels weird. When AI is involved, ask a grown-up to help you check—AI can be wrong.
2.parentBlurb: Theme: short-form video habits. Practice one “kind comment” role-play and one screen-time boundary together. And when AI is involved, ask a grown-up to help you check—AI can be wrong.

3.title: Snaps That Stay
3.story: SpArki packs messages into little glowing bottles. Some wash away; some stick around. This week is about who should see what — and asking a grown-up before sharing surprises. When you use AI, ask a grown-up to help you check—AI can be wrong.
3.parentBlurb: Theme: ephemerality vs screenshots. Remind: if it’s not okay in the kitchen, it’s not okay in chat. Remember to ask a grown-up to help you check AI ideas—AI can be wrong.

4.title: Blocks, Buddies, and Boundaries
4.tagline: Play worlds, kind teammates, and safe exits.
4.story: SpArki builds with colorful blocks — and meets other builders online. Kids practice kind teamwork, reporting icky behavior, and stepping away when play stops feeling safe. If AI is part of the lesson, ask a grown-up to help you check—AI can be wrong.
4.parentBlurb: Theme: multiplayer kindness and reporting. Co-create one family rule for online games. When AI is involved, ask a grown-up to help you check because AI can be wrong.

5.title: Victory Without Meanness
5.tagline: Competition, trash talk, and resetting after a loss.
5.story: SpArki drops into a bright battle world where winning feels huge — and losing stings. Kids learn that everyone loses sometimes, meanness isn’t a skill, and breaks are brave. When AI is involved, ask a grown-up to help you check—AI can be wrong.
5.parentBlurb: Theme: competitive games and emotions. Model losing gracefully once this week — kids notice. When AI is involved, ask a grown-up to help you check because AI can be wrong.

6.title: Forums, Facts, and Fiction
6.tagline: Threads, rumors, and checking with a grown-up.
6.story: SpArki finds a wall of notes — some true, some silly, some mean. Kids practice slowing down, not spreading rumors, and asking a trusted adult when something feels off. When AI is part of the learning, ask a grown-up to help you check—AI can be wrong.
6.parentBlurb: Theme: forums and misinformation. Try “pause and verify” as a household habit. When AI is involved, ask a grown-up to help you check—AI can be wrong.

7.title: Return to the Kind Grid
7.story: SpArki revisits the photo grid with fresh eyes — patterns are easier the second time. Kids strengthen habits: pause, kindness, and asking for help. When AI is involved, ask a grown-up to help you check—AI can be wrong.
7.parentBlurb: Spiral review week. Celebrate one safety habit your child improved since week 1. When AI is involved, ask a grown-up to help you check because AI can be wrong.

8.title: Sparki’s Two-World Bridge
8.tagline: Connect safety habits with how AI helpers work.
8.story: SpArki builds a bridge between the safety world and the AI lab. Kids see that tools can help — and that people still choose kindness, privacy, and fairness. When AI is involved, ask a grown-up to help you check—AI can be wrong.
8.parentBlurb: Integration week: link “ask a grown-up” from safety with “AI can be wrong” from AI literacy. Remember to check AI ideas with a grown-up when you’re unsure.
